title: A Jet Lost Its Roof at 24,000 Feet and Still Landed

scenes.text: A passenger jet once lost part of its roof at 24,000 feet.
April 1988, over Hawaii. An 18 foot section of the cabin ceiling tore away in flight.
Passengers could see the open sky above them. One flight attendant was swept out and never found.
The pilots flew on and landed on the island of Maui.
The plane was almost 19 years old. Metal fatigue had worn it down.
Everyone else survived. The roof was gone. The plane still flew.

description:
In April 1988, Aloha Airlines Flight 243 lost about 18 feet of its upper cabin at 24,000 feet and still landed on Maui.
One flight attendant was lost. The Boeing 737 was nearly 19 years old, and metal fatigue was to blame. The pilots landed at Kahului Airport and everyone else on board survived, though dozens were injured.
Would you have stayed calm? Tell us below.
first_comment: This one flight changed how airlines inspect old planes. Would you fly on a 19 year old jet?
